prompt: I've got two weeks starting Dec 1 and I'm honestly burnt out. I want somewhere chill and tropical, warm water, maybe finally learn to surf properly, great food, NOT a party scene. Flying from Boston, around $3k all in.

text: Burnt out + tropical + learn to surf: I'll assume solo, mid-range.

output.travel_style: Slow travel, 2-3 bases max; mid-range comfort; assumed solo traveler

text: Thinking Pacific Costa Rica, Caribbean Panama and Siargao. Checking each one.
December is dry season in Nicoya but wet in Bocas and Siargao. That changes things.

options.name: Nicoya Peninsula
options.why: Laid-back surf towns (Nosara, Santa Teresa, Sámara) with gentle beginner breaks, yoga culture and great sodas. Dry season just starting.
options.weather_summary: Avg high 31°C / low 23°C, 2 of 15 days with rain, ~8 h sunshine/day
options.tradeoffs: Dirt roads between towns; Santa Teresa pricier than it used to be.

options.name: Bocas del Toro
options.why: Caribbean islands on stilts, calm bays, cheap and very slow-paced.
options.weather_summary: Avg high 29°C / low 24°C, 8 of 15 days with rain, ~5 h sunshine/day
options.tradeoffs: December is wet on the Caribbean side; Bocas Town has a party strip.

options.name: Siargao
options.why: Palm-jungle island with a soft surf scene and incredible island-hopping.
options.weather_summary: Avg high 29°C / low 24°C, 11 of 15 days with rain, ~4 h sunshine/day
options.tradeoffs: Peak rainy season in December and ~2 days lost to travel each way.

output.reasoning: Nicoya wins on what matters most for a burnt-out traveler in December: dry-season sun, beginner surf, and a 6.5 h flight. Siargao is the dreamiest vibe but rain and a 22 h journey would eat the trip; Bocas is cheapest but wet this time of year.

text: Three bases running down the coast, ending close to LIR.

flights.route: BOS → LIR (1 stop via MIA/ATL) round trip
flights.notes: Estimate for early December; book ~6 weeks out. LIR is much closer than SJO.

output.getting_around: Shared and private shuttles between towns (no car needed); bikes and walking within each town.
